summary: The site of Mission Rock's only permitted stand-alone parking structure, a 100-ft-max garage on the Bridgeview Street side of Block D sized in the EIR at about 2,300 spaces (837,200 gsf) to replace Giants event parking. The Port's October 2023 memo says 'Phase 2 will include the parking garage' and that the Garage Report was submitted on October 14, 2022; the memo does not name Parcel D2, so the link to this block comes from the Design Controls, which allow stand-alone above-grade parking only here. Phase 2 was slowed in 2023. The Port's June 2026 staff memo on up to $10 million for Phase 2 pre-development does not mention the garage; the Commission's minutes record that item (Resolution 26-34) as passed unanimously on June 9, 2026.

milestones.text: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock DDA and Design Controls that set this block's use and envelope (among Resolutions 18-03 to 18-10, which the Jan 30, 2018 minutes record as adopted)

The Notice of Determination gives March 6, 2018 as the date the City 'decided to carry out or approve the project' and lists the Board of Supervisors' final actions, including File No. 171286 (affirming the Planning Department's certification of the Final EIR) and File No. 180092 (the DDA); it was filed March 9, 2018. The Board's own records date two of the other approvals earlier: Resolution 42-18 (the DDA, File 180092) was adopted February 13, 2018, and Ordinance 33-18 (the Development Agreement, File 171313) was finally passed February 27, 2018. The Port's Oct 2023 report calls No. 33-18 a Resolution and its June 2026 report an Ordinance; the Board's file shows an ordinance

Development Agreement takes effect (the Port's fact sheet lists the DA effective date as Aug. 15, 2018, with a 30-year term and 4 phases); the Planning page dates both the Development Agreement and the DDA 8/15/2018
Draft EIR sizes the Block D2 structure at 2,300 spaces and 837,200 gsf, within a project maximum of 3,100 spaces

The Potrero View (published January 13, 2018) reports that construction would be undertaken in four phases and that 'In the second phase, two more blocks would be developed, plus a 10-level parking structure, which’ll allow for continuous Giants parking'
Developer submits the Garage Report defining the Phase 2 garage's parameters; reviewed and signed off by SFMTA and Planning
Developer sends the Port its Phase 2 Submittal (with a Garage Report submitted October 14, 2022 and a Basis of Design November 18, 2022); the budget and appraisal elements are deferred

Port Commission adopts Resolution 23-46 (passed unanimously as amended, with non-substantive changes); its recitals state that Phase 2 is 'not currently financially feasible' and that Port and Developer staff 'mutually agreed earlier this year to decelerate work on Phase 2 while waiting for macroeconomic conditions to improve'

Port staff say later phases 'may require higher percentages of BMR units' to reach the project's 40% target after Phase 1 was cut to 132 BMR units; the Port, developer and MOHCD are reviewing changes 'with the goal of improving the feasibility of future Phases of Mission Rock and accelerating development' (Resolution 25-17)

Port Commission approves Resolution 26-34, authorizing up to $10 million in Port Capital as pre-development funding for Phase 2 (design/engineering for Phase 2 infrastructure and vertical buildings), intended to avoid a 12-18 month delay to construction readiness. Staff's schedule contemplates horizontal infrastructure and vertical building construction beginning as early as Summer/Fall 2027, but the memo's own Table 1 gives illustrative repayment scenarios for a 2027, 2028 or 2029 vertical construction start, contingent on the Developer securing anchor tenants -- not a committed date for this or any other Phase 2 block.

details.text: Use of Block D2: the Design Controls permit stand-alone above-grade parking nowhere else at Mission Rock, and the Land Use Chart lists residential, production, commercial and retail uses as not permitted on D2; Section 7.7.2 requires the structure to provide 'a minimum of 10,000 square feet of active uses, and/or transit related services at the ground floor'.

Interim parking at Block D2: this is a 2019 forecast. The 2019 Phase 1 submittal says Lot A (the remaining Seawall Lot 337 lot) 'could continue to accommodate 1,000 to 1,500 vehicles' pending future-phase construction, and Pier 48 'as many as 750 to 1,000 spaces', for Oracle Park events.
Phase 2 timing for Block D2: the Port's October 2023 repayment model used a hypothetical Phase 2 start of March 2026.

open_questions: The Garage Report's actual space count and levels are not in the Port memo; the report itself was not located.

A 2019 Phase 1 submittal placed the district energy plant on Parcel A rather than Block D: the developer's July 2, 2019 Phase 1 overview says 'We have tentatively planned for the Central DES to be in Parcel A due to its large footprint', and the Port's June 2026 report lists the 'District Energy System (heating and cooling) located in Parcel A'.

The Port's June 5, 2026 report schedules the Developer's Phase 2 Submittal ('proposal for Phase 2 including development summary and Phase budget') for Winter/Spring 2027 and a 'Potential Construction Start' for Summer/Fall 2027 (Table 2; expected dates, not events). No source read reports a construction start, a Phase 2 budget approval or a vertical design submittal for this block, and none states the block's current use; the Developer's July 2019 Phase 1 overview forecast that Lot A, the remainder of Seawall Lot 337, would keep serving parking pending future-phase construction.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.

The Port's January 26, 2018 staff report (Table 3, DDA Major Terms) describes the DDA's outside date for commencing construction of each later Phase as 'the earlier of 5 years after completion of vertical construction of the prior Phase or 14 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 2, 20 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 3, and 25 years after the Entitlement Date for Phase 4'. These are legal deadlines, not forecasts. The DDA text itself was not read, so no calendar date is derived here.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block D2. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The Port's fact sheet (updated June 24, 2021) lists 'Commence construction on Phase 2, including parking structure' among its five-year milestones, and the Port's October 2023 memo says 'Phase 2 will include the parking garage'. The DDA text itself (Board File 180092, adopted by the Board of Supervisors as Resolution 42-18 on February 13, 2018) was not read, so its Land Use Table and Schedule of Performance target dates are not cited here. Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023, per this record's own milestones. No later Port memo, Design Controls revision or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 2 or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports an expected-completion date for this block.

As of 2026-09-21: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (through Fall 2027 contractor procurement) and a 'potential' construction start as early as Summer/Fall 2027, but the memo explicitly frames 2027/2028/2029 as alternative scenarios depending on when the Developer secures anchor tenants, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.
The Port's June 2026 Phase 2 memo does not mention Block D2 or the garage, so no source says whether the garage is still planned as described in the 2023 memo.

Parking spaces at Block D2: the EIR gives about 2,300, with up to 700 more in a possible below-grade garage under Mission Rock Square; the DDA describes 3,000 structured spaces project-wide to serve the project and ballpark patrons.

Area of Block D2: the 97,498 sq ft (2.24 acres) figure is for Block D as a single block, from the March 2012 proposal's parcel table; that table predates the 2018 Design Controls' D1/D2 division and gives no D1/D2 split.
